title: Latency telemetry fusion region allocator with network-health escrow and model-variant fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: customer-facing requests sporadically experience region-level latency spikes that are not well-handled by the current coarse region selector. Existing logic treats p50 or last-sample latency in isolation and either over-reacts (excess cross-region failovers) or under-reacts (slow user experiences). We need a robust allocator that fuses percentile latency telemetry (p50/p95), continuous network health signals, and an escrow mechanism to avoid cascading failovers. It should also support deterministic fallback to compatible model variants (quantized/smaller variants) and tier-aware routing (hosted vs dedicated) based on policy.

Proposal: implement a telemetry-fusion region allocator that: 1) consumes streaming quantile telemetry (p50 and p95) and short-term EWMA of request latency per POP and per route; 2) computes a normalized network health score from packet loss, RTT jitter, and path error-rate; 3) fuses latency and net-health into a composite region score using configurable weights and temporal smoothing; 4) maintains an "escrow" credit for regions so brief transient spikes do not instantly trigger failover; 5) ties region-level degraded state to a fallback plan that prefers: a) same-region compatible model-variant (e.g., int8/4bit quantized), b) dedicated-tier variant within the same region, c) nearest healthy region respecting data residency policies; 6) provides grade-of-service policies so high-SLA customers preferentially route to dedicated pools and low-SLA traffic prioritizes cost and locality.

Algorithm details: - Telemetry ingestion: use current aggregator pipeline to emit rolling p50/p95 per 1m window and a per-second EWMA for last-request latency (alpha=0.25 default). - Net health derivation: composite_net = 1 - clamp(0,1, w_loss*loss_norm + w_rtt*rtt_norm + w_jitter*jitter_norm + w_err*err_rate_norm ). Normalization buckets based on historical 99th percentiles per POP. - Composite score = w_latency*latency_score + w_net*(1 - composite_net) where latency_score combines normalized p95 and p50 (default w_p95=0.7, w_p50=0.3) mapped to [0,1] with configurable thresholds. - Escrow: regions accrue grace credit when healthy and spend credit while above thresholds; only drop region out of rotation when escrow <= 0 and composite score > degrade_threshold. Escrow refill rate and initial credit are configurable per tier. - Cooldown/circuit-breaker: on eviction, start cooldown of 60s * backoff_factor (exponential up to 30m). - Fallback mapping: define policy table per model family mapping candidate variants and compatibility checks (tokenizer/precision). If same-region variant unavailable, attempt nearest-region reroute respecting SLO and data residency.

Observability and safety: emit region score history, escrow levels, decision trace for each routed request, and an aggregated SLA impact metric. Add synthetic canary requests to validate pathing. Default thresholds conservative to minimize blowups.

Why different from existing work: many tickets focus on percentile-based ranking or network link penalties only. This ticket operationalizes an escrow credit and explicit model-variant fallback plan combined into a single allocator that is tier-aware and safe to roll out incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for composite score computation with synthetic telemetry vectors (edge cases for normalization and clamping)
Integration test in staging demonstrating: stable routing during 90s transient p95 spike when escrow > 0, and failover when persistent degradation persists (>5m)
End-to-end canary that verifies fallback to compatible quantized model variant for a simulated region outage
Dashboards instrumented: region_score_timeseries, escrow_balance, fallback_count_by_model_variant, SLA_error_budget_consumption
No >5% regression in median latency for control traffic during staged rollout (per-route dashboards)

Implement composite scoring module and escrow manager in runtime routing service

Unit tests + property tests for score boundaries
Staging integration test with synthetic spike generator and canary runner
